look_here_first: FIRST flip a mature leaf: tiny NECTARY DOTS on UNDERSIDE = affinis; lutea has none. Both affinis and lutea lack PETIOLE glands, so don't confuse the structures. Next check small bracts under an open flower: affinis has them, lutea lacks them. Affinis's green-yellow flower is generally >25 mm wide, with wavy, clubbed outer corona tips (>10 mm). The broad cowboy-hat leaf is only a clue.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — published specimen/distribution records; Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index and Balcones Canyonlands Preserve list; Bexar — documented native occurrence in San Antonio/Bexar County and central Texas county distribution.

best_field_traits: leaves broader than long, usually 2–3 rounded lobes
outer corona filaments long and sinuous
nectaries present on abaxial leaf surface
morphology_keys.comparison_training: P. lutea lacks floral bracts and abaxial leaf nectaries and has smaller flowers. P. foetida is much hairier, foul-smelling when rubbed, and has a conspicuous cage of finely divided involucral bracts around the flower/fruit.
